egress.terms: Billed per byte: '$0.50 per GB on standard hosts', plus hosts count x3. Plans carry a monthly quota - Pro 15 GB/month, Premium 40 GB/month - with overage at $0.40 and $0.30/GB. A per-host daily bandwidth is also published for five hosts.
egress.free_allowance: Pro 15 GB/month, Premium 40 GB/month; pay-as-you-go credits from $2

record.interface_detail: No public API documentation was found: /api answers 404. The service is a web flow, and the per-host table is published as an HTML status page.
record.tooling: No documented API, no rclone backend; automation would need a browser session. That is a note about tooling, not a verdict.
record.chaining: The only service here that prices egress per byte, so it can absorb a one-off overflow when a capped host blocks elsewhere on a flat-rate plan.

limits.value: Pro 15 GB/month, Premium 40 GB/month, overage USD 0.40-0.30/GB
512 MB per file on the free tier
per host per day: NitroFlare 100 GB, FileBoom 50 GB, Keep2Share 50 GB, Upstore 20 GB, FileJoker 15 GB

record.limits_note: The status table has a Daily bandwidth column for 61 hosts and only 5 carry a number; the rest print an em dash, which the vendor leaves undefined.
record.binding_note: 40 GB/month on Premium is 1.3 GB/day, or 3.6% of the 36.7 GB/day 1 TiB of monthly transfer needs; the plan quota binds about 27x before any host cap does.

identity_cost.detail: Not read: no signup form was opened. Free plan needs no payment; credits are bought with a card.

record.reliability_note: Five hosts are marked 'Partner network' rather than 'Own account', and two Plus hosts (FileJoker, Upstore) have 'never' in the last-checked column, so the published cap is a policy figure rather than an observed one for those.
record.confidence_note: Both tables are the vendor's own pages read. The 5 published caps are policy statements; a paid download would be needed to confirm enforcement.

evidence.proved: 61-row table with Host, Availability, Served by, Status, 7-day success, Class, Daily bandwidth; 5 numeric caps, the rest em dash
'2 files a day, up to 512 MB each' free, '$0.50 per GB', Pro '$4.99 per month 15 GB', Premium '$9.99 40 GB'
'every host has its own published daily bandwidth per user, reset at 00:00 UTC'

record.notes: The site is new enough that its own comparison guides are the clearest statement of the cap policy; the status table is the machine-readable version.

card.category: hosted debrid bot (file-host link to download link)
card.summary: The pricing page's Free column: '2 files a day, up to 512 MB each', 'Standard hosts only', 'Same verified downloads as paid'.

record.category: hosted debrid bot (file-host link to download link)

free_tier.stated: The pricing page's Free column: '2 files a day, up to 512 MB each', 'Standard hosts only', 'Same verified downloads as paid'.
free_tier.notes: 512 MB is a per-file cap, so the free ceiling is at most 2 x 512 MB a day

per_object_cap.stated: 512 MB per file on the free tier; a paid plan has no published per-file cap on this page.

retention.stated: 'Paid links last 72 hours, free ones 24 hours.' The linked copy itself is deleted on that clock; nothing is stored in Telegram.
retention.notes: the day count is the free-link lifetime, the shortest published one

egress.terms: No Telegram traffic at all: 'Does the bot send the file through Telegram? No. It sends a download link to our verified copy, which works in a browser or a download manager and supports resume.'
egress.free_allowance: none: every byte past the free allowance is billed
egress.price_per_tb: $0.50/GB standard hosts; $0.40/GB overage on Pro; $0.30/GB on Premium

record.interface_detail: A Telegram chat plus a Mini App; the same account also has a website and an API.
record.tooling: Any Telegram client. No token: 'Starting @debridmasterbot creates your DebridMaster account - no email or password needed.'
record.chaining: Fetches a file-host link and hands back a resumable direct URL, so the byte path bypasses Telegram; useful when the object is on Keep2Share or FileJoker and useless as a Telegram store.

limits.value: 512 MB per file on the free tier

record.binding_note: A two-per-day count fails first: two 512 MB files is about 1 GB/day, and the counter stops it before any byte quota could.

identity_cost.detail: The account is created by pressing Start in Telegram; an email is optional and there is no card at signup. Paying needs crypto or Telegram Stars, 'The minimum top-up in the bot is $5'.

record.reliability_note: Plus hosts (FileJoker, FilesMonster, Upstore) count triple against quota, and dead links are not charged; the bot's copy is deleted with the link, so a re-download after 24 hours costs again.
record.confidence_note: Prices, free allowance and the no-Telegram-delivery answer are all on the vendor's own pages read. Nothing was purchased or measured.

evidence.proved: '2 files a day, up to 512 MB each' on the free column; '$0.50 per GB' pay-as-you-go; Pro '$4.99 per month' with '15 GB per month'; Premium '$9.99 per month' with '40 GB per month'
'Does the bot send the file through Telegram? No. It sends a download link to our verified copy' and 'Paid links last 72 hours, free ones 24 hours.'
'Starting @debridmasterbot creates your DebridMaster account - no email or password needed.' and 'The minimum top-up in the bot is $5'

record.price_per_tb_month: USD 500 (pay-as-you-go, 0.50/GB); USD 250 effective on Premium (40 GB for 9.99)
record.notes: The important fact for debrid is negative: this class of bot is a debrid front-end in a chat and moves zero bytes through Telegram. Abandon if the free column changes or if the bot starts uploading files into the chat.
